slides.title: Failed rains hit 3.5 million people
slides.body: A new IFRC drought assessment, reported by The Reporter

slides.title: woredas affected across six regions
slides.body: El Niño delayed the June-September rains by up to four weeks in parts of the north, east and southeast, the IFRC says.

slides.title: community ponds still held water
slides.body: In West Hararghe, Oromia, an estimated 696,873 people across 15 woredas urgently need help.

slides.title: children with severe acute malnutrition
slides.body: found in a June screening of 464,880 children in West Hararghe, plus 24,925 with moderate malnutrition.

slides.title: people need assistance in Tigray
slides.body: across seven assessed woredas. In North Gondar, Amhara, 318,443 people are affected and 19,318 displaced.

slides.title: of those affected are covered by the response
slides.body: The Ethiopian Red Cross plans to reach 50,000 people by March 2027, the IFRC notes.

slides.title: Let aid reach every drought-hit family.
slides.body: Follow for sourced updates from across Ethiopia.
